recipes.name: Cajun Dirty Rice
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chile peppers

steps.text: In a skillet over medium heat, brown the ground beef, sausage, and onion; drain.

In a large pan, combine rice mix and 2 cups water. Add diced tomatoes and chilies. Stir in the kidney beans. Bring to a boil, then add meat mixture. Season with salt and pepper. Return to boil, reduce heat, and cover, stirring occasionally. Cook for 25 minutes, until rice is easily fluffed with a fork.

raw_recipe.headline: Cajun Dirty Rice
raw_recipe.description: One of our family’s all-time favorites. Make it as spicy or mild as you please. It is hearty on a cold winter’s night. If you are cooking for a crowd, this recipe can easily be doubled. Be sure to serve this with cornbread!

review.reviewBody: I absolutely ADORE this recipe!! I double the recipe and take to parties. I usually cut back on the ground beef a little bit. When I double the recipe I usually only use 1 1/2 pounds ground beef. I also use one can milder Rotel and one can regular Rotel, so that it's not too spicy. I also recommend starting the onion with a little garlic before throwing in the meat...YUM!

Wonderful...I did what others did....used two boxes of dirty rice and 4 cups of Chicken broth. I browned the hot pork sausage, cut up a lb of hot link sausage and dumped it all in the crockpot. Yes, it does smell weird when its cooking. After 4 hours.....great. Will make again. Dont add any extra salt....pretty salty. I did tweek it with some tabasco......

This Louisiana girl and her Texan husband loved this dish. It will definitely get saved. I followed other opinions here to substitute water for chicken broth. I also used Emeril's Seasoning & a little Cayenne Pepper while browning the meat and had spicy sausage on hand. My husband commented that it had a nice kick to it. I will definitely make again and possibly use in the future for a pot luck. 

I will agree though with another poster that it's A LOT of food. For 2 people, we still had 2/3 a pot full of food when I put it away last night. Will cut in half next time I make for just us.
We doubled the rice, tomatoes and water to stretch the meal out further and cut the sausage into small bites as well. My family loved this recipe and we will make it again.

EXCELLENT... we loved this! I too made some changes which is why I only gave it four stars. I sautee'd garlic with the onion and burger as suggested by another review. I used two boxes of Zataran's dirty rice mix, two cans of mild rotel, four cups chicken broth and one cup of water. I also used one can of black beans (rinsed) instead of kidney beans and a cup of corn. I only used 12 oz of beef sausage because that's how it came and I didn't want to buy two. Before it was done cooking I added six ounces of Velveeta cheese. I think the final product had a great flavor and a nice balance of rice and meat. My husband loved it and it made plenty for left overs the next day.
I did not add bean however I added 1/2 cup of rice and lonely 1/2 of the meat. Used chicken broth and a few piquillo peppers. It turned out delicious.

Made this to accompany a 4th of July Shrimp Boil. Used 2 packages of Dirty Rice based on an earlier comment, added an additional cup of water to accommodate the extra rice, used only 1/2 lb ground beef and used mild pork sausage instead of beef. Very tasty and had a bit of spice to it, even though I used mild pork sausage and mild Rotel. The result easily filled a 3 quart casserole dish. Will definitely keep this recipe on hand!

absolutely delicious! thank you for sharing. i made only some minor changes: i used kielbasa, added diced green peppers and minced garlic, and omitted the salt & pepper (only because i forgot to add it, but turns out that it didn't need any extra salt or pepper for my taste). i also cooked the ground beef and kielbasa separately so that they browned better. will definitely make again!

I will be making this again! This was easy and delicious! I did make a few changes since my family likes spicy food. I substituted the habanero Rotel tomatoes for the regular and I substituted the regular smoked sausage for the cajun seasoned Andouille sausage. It was even better the next day!

Great week-night dinner! Instead of 2 8-oz. boxes of rice mix, I used 1 12-oz. box. To cut down on fat content, I used 1 lb. of 96% lean ground beef & 1 lb. skinless chicken breast, chopped. When I browned the meat & onion, I seasoned w/ Emeril's Essence. I also used dark & light kidney beans

The best dirty, red beans and rice we've ever had. We have a ton of deer sausage and ground meat left over from the hunting season, so I added both of those to the mixture. I just browned the ground meat, and sliced the sausage into pieces. It turned out to be a dirty, red beans and rice. It was fabulous and so easy to make! I wouldn't tell her, but I bet I could go head to head with my New Orleans grandmother with this recipe! ;)
Added shrimp scampi including half the sauce and this rocks!

Mama liked it! I used pinto beans instead of kidney beans and added celery. I followed the suggestion to use chicken broth instead of water. Next time I might back off on the beans by one can and maybe add some bell pepper.

This recipe has become a household favorite. I use "Slap ya Mama" Cajun seasoning in it and some splashes of Tabasco sauce for a little extra seasoning, and it turns out great. I'm actually making it for dinner tonight.
Really good and I added some small shrimp, okra and another 4oz of rice.

I only had one pound of hamburger and that was plenty of meat. Other than that I made it exactly as called for and it was a huge hit. Even my somewhat picky son took one bite and said "this is really good" . Who cares if its not what some of you call dirty rice. It's yummy.
I MADE THIS! DELICIOUS!! THE WHOLE FAMILY LOVED IT
Awesomeness! Followed it to a T.
I'm sorry, but this is not "cajun" dirty rice. Closer to a jambalaya.
